notes: v1.14.570 — NO INVENTED NUMBER SHOWN AS A BENCHMARK. PUNCHLIST P-2, ruling (a). One visible change: the stall nudge read '404 min on POWER (typical: 60 min). Unlogged blocker?' and now reads '404 min on POWER · no baseline yet. Unlogged blocker?'. The 404 was measured; the 60 was invented, and the two sat side by side in one sentence with nothing telling a tech which was which. Contract B10. ⭐ THE DISTINCTION PHASE 0 FOUND, AND IT CHANGES THE RULING'S SHAPE: the constant did TWO jobs — it was the trigger threshold (elapsedMins > baseline * 2) AND the displayed comparison. Labelling the nudge 'no baseline yet' while an invented baseline still decided when to speak would have been a WORSE honesty position than before. A threshold deciding when to ask a question is not a claim about what is typical, so the trigger stays and only the display goes. ⛔ THE NUMBER NO LONGER LEAVES THE FUNCTION: deploy_checkPhaseAnomaly returns only elapsedMins now. Dropping it from the rendered string alone would have left a fabricated number in the data flow for the next consumer to pick up and print. ⚠ RENAMED PHASE_BASELINE_MINS to PHASE_STALL_TRIGGER_MINS — zero visible change, but 'baseline' is precisely the word that invited it to be rendered as data, and a misleading name with a careful comment twenty lines away is how this defect happened in the first place. ⭐ PHASE 0 ALSO FOUND THAT RULING (b) IS CLOSER THAN THE PUNCH LIST ASSUMED: real durations are already recordable — PHASE_STARTED carries a ts and is already read by this very detector, PHASE_COMPLETE is written at :31951 and read at :27308 and :30896, and phase records carry signedOffAt. The detector walks the audit log for the start and then reaches for a hardcoded constant instead of the matching completion. (b)'s real prerequisite is not 'five completions' but proving the start-to-complete pairing is sound: matching is by STRING SEARCH on e.summary for phase label plus rack name, not by id, and that robustness is unmeasured. Reported, not built.
